competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight markets leaned defensive: the dollar firmed across G10, commodity currencies sold off, and safe-haven demand kept oil and gold supported despite softer equity sentiment. WTI futures marked near $80/bbl, Brent near $89, and gold near $3,651/oz; the Dow sat near 49,595 with implied volatility still in the mid-30s. ECB rhetoric turned more hawkish as Governing Council members argued tightening remains prudent while price pressures broaden beyond energy. In contrast, Australian bonds extended their rally on mounting bets the RBA’s next move is a cut, amplified by a weaker nominal growth outlook in the upcoming budget update. Energy logistics around the Strait of Hormuz stay in focus after questionable tanker tracking and prior Hormuz incidents. Positioning still reflects expectations of further Fed tightening even as equities struggle. Up next: euro-area and US inflation and activity data, plus any central-bank speak. Several macro consumer and labor series in our research set remain thinly covered.

postmortems.what_worked: The long isolated hawkish ECB commentary against an offered Australian dollar, and euro-aussie is still the 20-session upside break at 1.6532 after the close.

causal.original_belief: The long euro-aussie was the clean non-dollar expression of hawkish ECB commentary against an Australian dollar already breaking down versus Canada and New Zealand.

causal.assumptions_right: The Australian dollar stayed the offered leg, and ECB speakers still want tighter policy.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The close treated a Canada rotation as a replacement and underweighted that the original cross could keep the break without that rotation.
causal.causal_divergence: The expression was rotated off a working euro-aussie long, so the seat is flat while both the euro-aussie break and the Australia-Canada break continued.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same hawkish ECB remarks and the offered Australian dollar, the long would have stayed on rather than being closed for a cross that is not the booked risk.
causal.future_implication: Keep the non-dollar policy wedge in the cross that has the opposite central-bank talk, and do not close it merely to rotate into Canada.

postmortems.expression_assessment: Short USDCAD was the right spot expression of a Canada valuation view, and closing it at an unchanged 1.43 left the later one-year extreme unowned. That was an expression swap, and the closed ticket is not reopened at 1.4362.
postmortems.no_new_lesson: The unchanged 1.43 round trip and the later extension to the one-year high are bounded variance around an expression swap that left the book flat. The process remains sound because a covered Canada short does not inherit a new percentile.

causal.original_belief: USDCAD was rich enough to hold a short entered near 1.43, wrong if crude repriced to a scare that made that level fair or if spot stayed pinned there for about 20 sessions.
causal.observed_reality: The short was closed on 23 November after about three days with entry and exit both near 1.43. USDCAD is now 1.4362, a one-year extreme and the 20-session high.
causal.assumptions_right: Spot was the right vehicle for a Canada valuation view, and the crude-scare clause was the correct kill-switch for that ticket.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: A three-day hold was short relative to a one-year valuation gap, and leaving at an unchanged price underweighted how far the percentile could extend after the ticket was closed.
causal.causal_divergence: The close was an expression swap at the entry price, not convergence. The gap then widened while the book no longer owned it.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: The entry rule would still have been short until a 20-session pin or a crude scare. That same rule does not create a fresh short at 1.4362 once the ticket is closed.
causal.future_implication: Leave USDCAD flat. A new dollar-Canada value short needs its own anchor and does not inherit this closed ticket just because the percentile is now more extreme.
